rows.grounds: instrument by which the Lord acts
power characterized as the body of reflective awareness
power not different in form from the Lord's own self

items.question: By what power does the Lord manifest a nature not other than his own self?
premises: The Lord acts through power.
This power is embodied as reflective awareness.
This power is not other than the Lord's own self.
items.inference: The Lord's manifestation is grounded in a power identical with his own reflective self-nature.
items.plain_english: By his power, whose body is reflective awareness and whose form is not other than his own self, the Lord acts.

rows.grounds: the cosmic drama consisting of five acts
one who relishes the aesthetic essence

items.question: What role does the Lord assume in the great drama of the five cosmic acts?
premises: There is a great drama of five acts.
The Lord engages in this drama.
He engages as a connoisseur relishing it.
items.inference: The Lord's cosmic activity is a playful, aesthetic enjoyment of the fivefold drama.
items.plain_english: The Lord, as a connoisseur, plays in the great drama of the five acts.

rows.grounds: between the universe and the one whose body is the universe

items.question: Is there any essential difference between the universe and the one whose body is the universe?
premises: The universe and its embodied form are considered together.
Difference could be merely apparent or essential.
No essential difference exists between them.
items.inference: The universe and the one embodied as the universe are essentially non-different.
items.plain_english: There is no essential difference whatsoever between the universe and the one whose body is the universe.

rows.grounds: because of the connection between being and manifestation
the appearance or shining of being

items.question: On what basis can the appearance of being be affirmed in that context?
premises: Being and manifestation are connected.
This connection grounds the appearance of being.
The appearance of being is thus affirmed there.
items.inference: The appearance of being is established through the inseparable connection of being and manifestation.
items.plain_english: If considered there, the appearance of being arises indeed from the connection between being and manifestation.

rows.grounds: easily obtained through the attainment of one's own nature
of that which is not a real entity

items.question: Can a non-entity possess a relation easily obtained through its own nature?
premises: A relation is easily obtained through attaining one's own nature.
A non-entity lacks its own nature.
Therefore a non-entity cannot have such a relation.
items.inference: Only a real entity, not a non-entity, can sustain a relation grounded in its own nature.
items.plain_english: For a relation easily obtained through the attainment of one's own nature cannot belong to a non-entity.

rows.grounds: in a state of dependence or expectation

items.question: Can anything of this reality abide if it depends on external expectation?
premises: Abiding requires independence from expectation.
Dependence on expectation undermines stable existence.
Thus no abiding would be possible for it.
items.inference: This reality cannot have any abiding if it is made dependent on expectation.
items.plain_english: If there were dependence on expectation, there would not be any abiding of this at all.

rows.grounds: state of being insentient or inert

items.question: What consequence follows from not accepting the destruction of reality?
premises: Destruction of reality is not accepted.
Inertness is often attributed under such assumptions.
Even that inertness ceases under this view.
items.inference: Rejecting the destruction of reality also removes the basis for attributing inertness.
items.plain_english: When destruction is not accepted, even inertness ceases.

rows.grounds: set forth as the topic or established

items.question: Why does the established unity of consciousness with the world never cease?
premises: The preceding reasoning removes grounds for separation.
The unity of the world with consciousness is established.
This established unity does not cease.
items.inference: The world's unity with consciousness remains unceasing because no valid ground for its cessation remains.
items.plain_english: Therefore, the established unity of the world with consciousness does not cease.

items.question: Who can delimit the power of Śambhu who transcends the entire universe?
premises: Śambhu transcends the universe.
His power is being considered for limitation.
No one is capable of delimiting it.
items.inference: The power of the universe-transcending Śambhu is beyond all delimitation.
items.plain_english: Who can delimit the power of Śambhu, who transcends the universe?

rows.grounds: relative pronoun introducing anything in the world
goes beyond or is left over from

items.question: Can anything in this world exceed the light of consciousness?
premises: Anything whatsoever in this world is considered.
Light or consciousness is the basis of manifestation.
Nothing exceeds that light.
items.inference: Everything in the world is contained within and does not exceed the light of consciousness.
items.plain_english: And whatever exists in this world does not exceed the light of consciousness.

rows.grounds: of those whose attention is one-pointed

items.question: What serves as the witness to this truth for those with single-pointed attention?
premises: Some possess single-pointed attention.
This truth requires direct witnessing.
Their own mind alone serves as the witness.
items.inference: For the attentive, direct cognition itself is the sole witness to this truth.
items.plain_english: Here, the mind alone of those with single-pointed attention is the witness.

items.question: Why does the supreme light not require any lesser light for its illumination?
premises: The sun is a self-luminous light.
A lamp is a lesser source of light.
The sun does not require the lamp's light.
items.inference: Supreme self-luminous light is independent and does not depend on lesser lights.
items.plain_english: Indeed, the light of the sun does not require the light of a lamp.

items.question: How does everything become manifest in a stainless and expansive mirror?
premises: A mirror can be stainless and expansive.
Such a mirror reflects without obstruction.
Everything shines in it.
items.inference: In a pure, unobstructed medium, all things are clearly manifested.
items.plain_english: Indeed, in a stainless, expansive mirror, everything shines forth.

items.question: What is the nature of the pure principle that arises fivefold beyond darkness?
premises: At the beginning a principle arises.
This principle is pure-natured and beyond darkness.
It manifests in a fivefold manner.
items.inference: The primordial principle is pure, transcendent of darkness, and expressed fivefold.
items.plain_english: In the beginning, the pure-natured principle, beyond darkness, arose in a fivefold way.

rows.grounds: having the nature of letters from a to śa

items.question: What letter-natured principle was emitted by Śiva at the primordial stage?
premises: Śiva emitted a principle.
This principle has the nature of letters.
Its range spans from the initial to the final letter indicated.
items.inference: Śiva emitted a primordial principle constituted by the range of letters from a to śa.
uncertainties: The exact intended letter range of akṣa+ādi+śānta+varṇa+ātmā follows the traditional reading as a to śa.
items.plain_english: Indeed, that principle, having the nature of the letters from a to śa, was emitted by Śiva.

rows.grounds: preceded by māyā and having the nature of letters from va to ya

items.question: What is the letter-natured principle preceded by māyā in the emanative sequence?
premises: A principle is described in the emanative sequence.
It is preceded by māyā.
It has the nature of letters from va to ya.
items.inference: The described principle is the māyā-preceded reality constituted by the letters from va to ya.
uncertainties: The compound is given as a single fused token; internal segmentation follows the provided analysis.
items.plain_english: It is preceded by māyā and has the nature of the letters from va to ya.

rows.grounds: the group of five beginning with the ear
the group of five beginning with speech

items.question: Which fivefold groups and classes are enumerated in this emanative structure?
premises: A group of five beginning with the ear is named.
The nādi and ṇādi classes are named.
A group of five beginning with speech is named.
items.inference: The emanative structure includes the sense group, nādi and ṇādi classes, and the action group.
uncertainties: The precise technical scope of nādi and ṇādi is context-dependent in this tradition.
items.plain_english: There are the group of five beginning with the ear, the nādi and ṇādi groups, and the group of five beginning with speech.

rows.grounds: of the one wishing to create

items.question: What is identified as the first vibration of the Lord desiring to create?
premises: The Lord desires to create.
A first vibration arises in that desire.
This first vibration is remembered as Śiva-tattva.
items.inference: Śiva-tattva is the primordial vibration of the Lord's creative will.
items.plain_english: The first vibration of the Lord who desires to create is remembered as the Śiva principle.

items.question: How does the universe abide after being created by the Lord's own will?
premises: The universe is created by the Lord's own will.
It is veiled by I-ness.
It abides in that veiled condition.
items.inference: The self-willed creation abides as the universe veiled by the sense of I-ness.
items.plain_english: Created by his own will, the universe abides, having been veiled by I-ness.

items.question: Which principle is defined by seeing the universe as an object of this-ness?
premises: A principle sees the universe.
The universe is seen as this-ness.
That state is identified as Īśvara-tattva.
items.inference: Īśvara-tattva is the principle in which the universe is beheld as this.
items.plain_english: That indeed would be the Īśvara principle, seeing the universe as this.

rows.grounds: in things conceived as like one's own limbs

items.question: What principle is characterized by differentiating cognition among entities taken as one's own limbs?
premises: Entities are apprehended as like one's own limbs.
A cognition of differentiation arises among them.
This differentiating cognition is Māyā-tattva.
items.inference: Māyā-tattva is the differentiating cognition operating among entities otherwise related to oneself.
items.plain_english: Māyā-tattva is the differentiating cognition in entities conceived as like one's own limbs.

items.question: Who is designated as the transmigrating individual soul and experiencer in this account?
premises: A particular subject is under discussion.
This subject transmigrates and experiences.
It is called the individual soul.
items.inference: The transmigrating experiencer is identified as the individual soul.
items.plain_english: This alone is indeed called the transmigrating individual soul, the experiencer.

rows.grounds: due to the contraction of that
in the form of kalā and so on

items.question: What results from the contraction of that principle into the nature of kalā and others?
premises: That principle undergoes contraction.
Contraction yields limited forms.
These are regarded as kalā and so on.
items.inference: Through contraction, the principle is regarded as taking the limited forms beginning with kalā.
items.plain_english: By its contraction, they are regarded as contracted, having the nature of kalā and so forth.

rows.grounds: cause of knowing only a little

items.question: What causal roles are assigned to vidyā and rāga in the contracted condition?
premises: Vidyā is present in the contracted condition.
Vidyā causes limited knowing.
Rāga causes clinging.
items.inference: In contraction, vidyā functions as the cause of limited knowledge and rāga as the cause of clinging.
uncertainties: kiñcit+jñatā+hetū is taken as a dual predicate in form, applied to the pair of principles named.
items.plain_english: Vidyā is the cause of limited knowledge, and rāga is the cause of clinging.
